For example, TVH001 and BEL002 account for a combined total of over 230 order lines, dwarfing the activity of many others whose order counts are frequently just one or two. Alongside order volume, delivery reliability varies widely: BEL002, despite high volume, shows that only about a third of its deliveries fall within the window of "on time to 5 days early," while two-thirds are 1 to 2 days late. In contrast, suppliers such as ALD001 and ATL004 show a distribution across "on time," "1 to 2 days late," and, in the latter case, up to "3 to 7 days late," suggesting more inconsistency.

Several suppliers with moderate or low order counts exhibit significant late deliveries. === Report ===
The reporting obligations outlined in Section 1201(c) of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) are critical to ensuring transparency and oversight of federally funded transportation investments. The Department of Transportation (DOT) requires all recipients of High Speed Intercity Passenger Rail (HSIPR) and Transportation Investment Generating Economic Recovery (TIGER) awards to provide detailed accounts of both jobs created and the expenditures of ARRA funds. These requirements apply to all awards issued on or before January 31, 2012.

For reporting purposes, each award may represent either a single project or a group of activities, and commonly includes amendments intended to expand project scope, add federal contributions, or otherwise adjust initial agreements. Amendments are systematically referenced by extension of the original (“parent”) award number: for instance, a parent award concludes with “-00,” and subsequent amendments increment the final digits (e.g., “-01,” “-02,” etc.), always retaining the core identifying string. This organizational structure ensures that cumulative data reflects the full scope of federal participation associated with a given project or set of activities.

Recipients must incorporate information from sub-recipients and vendors, aggregate data for amendments under their respective parent awards, and ensure strict compliance and accuracy in submissions. As stipulated, cumulative data should cover the entire period from February 17, 2009, through January 31, 2012, unless specified otherwise. Direct recipients are expected to submit one comprehensive report for all awards, using the official template distributed by the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA). The instructions further clarify submission modalities, the expectation of corrections upon request, and the timelines for responding to queries or modifications by February 24, 2012 where required.

 자료는 국내 이커머스 시장 내 주요 플레이어들의 실질적인 거래 규모와 시장 내 위치를 수치로 증명하고 있습니다.

=== Report ===
A review of recent student assessment outcomes reveals significant variation in individual performance, as well as several patterns worth noting. Student grades range from a low of 54 to a high of 100, demonstrating a broad distribution. While some students performed exceptionally well, achieving scores at or above 97, others fell noticeably below the class median.

In particular, a large cluster of students scored in the high 80s, forming a clear modal band. For example, three students earned an identical score of 88, indicating either a shared strength in the evaluation criteria or perhaps the impact of a common instructional approach. Beyond the main cluster, there are standout achievements including one perfect score and two students achieving scores in the high 90s, further raising the overall mean.

Conversely, the lower end of the distribution consists of a few underperforming students, with scores such as 54 and 64, which may warrant targeted academic support. Given the range and spread, the data, as illustrated in ## Sheet: Sheet1

|   Student ID | Name   |   Grade |
|-------------:|:-------|--------:|

|        10002 | B      |      85 |
|        10003 | C      |      89 |
|        10004 | D      |      94 |
|        10005 | E      |      88 |
|        10006 | F      |      64 |

|        10010 | J      |      99 |
|        10011 | K      |     100 |
|        10012 | L      |      69 |
|        10013 | M      |      97 |
|        10014 | N      |      86 |
, suggest a generally strong collective performance punctuated by isolated instances of both exceptional achievement and notable struggle.

| Grade Range | Number of Students |
|-------------|-------------------|
| 90-100      | 3                 |
| 80-89       | 6                 |
| 70-79       | 1                 |
| 60-69       | 2                 |
| 50-59       | 1                 |

=== Report ===
The proper processing of `<Sites>` and `<DistrictWide>` tag entries within the header of Staff and Student XML files is foundational for accurate and efficient data management in the context of district and site-level record updates. The structural and logical rules governing the use of these tags ensure both data integrity and compliance with validation requirements.

Among the most critical constraints, only one of the tag options—either `<Sites>` or `<DistrictWide>`—is permitted in the header. Including both simultaneously, or omitting both, will immediately lead to a file format error, as flagged during schema validation. Similarly, misuse or incomplete specification within either tag, such as including an empty `<DistrictWide>`, a non-zero site in `<DistrictWide>`, or referencing the special "000" district-wide site improperly within `<Sites>`, will also produce format errors and prevent further processing.

When the `<Sites>` tag is used appropriately, the application examines each site listed. Should a site's corresponding data be present in the XML file, the provided data completely replaces any existing data for that site within the application. In cases where a site is listed but not included in the file, the effect is a deletion—all previous records for that site are removed. This mechanism allows for precise, site-specific updates or removals, with any sites excluded from the list remaining unaffected. If there is an inconsistency—such as data present for a site not listed in `<Sites>`—the process is halted with an error.

Conversely, the `<DistrictWide>` tag, valid only when set to "000," governs bulk updates or removals across all district sites. The behavior here is nuanced depending on which sites have corresponding data:
- If data is supplied for all sites, the new data wholly replaces the current records across the district.
- If only a subset of sites is included, those records are updated while data for missing sites is purged.

A critical aspect of library services highlighted is the responsiveness to user feedback regarding facilities and operations. Please extract the detailed marketing campaign performance data including sent messages, opens, clicks, orders, and unsubscribes by offer and campaign phase from the report into JSON following the given structure. Format the data to clearly represent each offer’s metrics across the various campaign waves for easy comparative analysis.

=== Report ===
An analysis of recent marketing communications reveals distinct performance patterns across multiple offer campaigns targeting the same recipient segment. The campaigns exhibit varying levels of engagement, as measured by key indicators including the volume of sent messages, open rates, click-throughs, order completions, and unsubscribes.

The initial offer campaign, distributed over a diverse portfolio of five distinct offers, demonstrated that the fifth offer garnered the highest volume of sends, with 11,813 messages dispatched, substantially higher than the others, which ranged from approximately 1,600 to 4,300 messages. Despite this large outreach in offer five, the open rates remained relatively moderate, peaking at 2,412 opens for that offer, followed by the fourth offer with 1,555 opens. Interestingly, the click-to-open ratios fluctuate considerably; for instance, offer four recorded 495 clicks from 1,555 opens—a strong engagement—contrasted with offer three's modest clicks of 175 despite 1,350 opens.

Regarding conversion to orders, the second offer stands out with a remarkable 45 orders out of 1,117 opens and 383 clicks, implying a notably effective call to action or product-market fit relative to others. All other offers produced considerably fewer orders, with the highest after the second offer being 22 orders from offer five. Unsubscription rates, an indicator of potential audience fatigue or dissatisfaction, varied significantly. Offers with high messaging volume, specifically offer five, also saw elevated unsubscribes (24), while offers two, three, and four ranged between 0 and 9 unsubscribes, suggesting a correlation between volume and churn risk.

Subsequent offer campaigns (Offers 2 through 7) were more limited in scope. Offer 2 included two primary offers with combined sends exceeding 24,000 messages. This campaign, however, saw a relatively low order tally given the volume, with only 3 and 8 orders respectively for offers one and two within that campaign. Unsubscribe rates in this batch rose sharply, totaling 27, 50, and 72 unsubscribes corresponding to the “Actual #s,” offer one, and offer two.

Offers 3 through 7 each focused exclusively on a single offer, consistently sending 1,754 messages per offer, yielding around 446 opens and 56 clicks each, but generating only 3 orders per offer and virtually no unsubscribes recorded. This consistency might reflect a controlled experimental approach or repeated targeting of a niche segment to reinforce messaging.

Collectively, these data points underscore the importance of balancing outreach magnitude with audience tolerance and engagement depth. Large send volumes don’t consistently translate into higher conversion rates and may produce unwanted unsubscribe responses if campaign messaging is not closely aligned with recipients’ interests.
